# Motley Play

> Original logic puzzle books, interactive mystery games, and constraint-verified Kakuro solving & construction guides by Motley Play.

Last updated: 2026-11-10

About the author: [About Motley Play & Our Puzzle Engineering Methodology](https://motleyplay.com/about/)

## Advanced Kakuro Tactics

- [The Ultimate Guide to Advanced Kakuro Tactics](https://motleyplay.com/posts/advanced-kakuro-tactics-guide/): Advanced Kakuro tactics in one place: 2-to-5 cell magic blocks, ceiling/floor intersections, the 45 rule (innies/outies), and parity forcing chains.
- [Kakuro Magic Blocks Cheat Sheet: All 16 Unique Sums (2 to 5 Cells)](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-magic-blocks/): Complete reference table of all 16 Kakuro magic blocks across 2, 3, 4, and 5 cells. Learn how 4-cell and 5-cell unique sums cap crossing runs on hard grids.
- [Mastering the 45 Rule in Kakuro](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-45-rule/): Kakuro has no 3x3 boxes, so the Sudoku 45 rule needs a twist. Learn the 45-minus-clue long-entry trick and how innies and outies crack open isolated blocks.
- [Kakuro Intersection Logic: Ceilings, Floors, and High-Low Crossings](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-intersection-logic/): Master advanced Kakuro intersection logic: calculate ceiling and floor bounds for long entries, eliminate 'too big' and 'too small' candidates, and force corners.
- [Eliminating Guesswork in Kakuro: Parity and Logic](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-eliminating-guesswork/): Stop guessing on expert Kakuro puzzles. Use odd/even parity rules, ghost duplicates, and short forcing chains to resolve 2x2 pockets with pure deduction.

## Kakuro for Beginners

- [The Complete Beginner's Guide to Solving Kakuro](https://motleyplay.com/posts/beginner-kakuro-guide/): New to Kakuro? Learn to read diagonal sum clues, spot the 16 unique magic blocks that start every solve, and cross-reference intersections with zero guesswork.
- [Understanding Kakuro Rules and Grid Mechanics](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-rules-grid-mechanics/): Learn the Kakuro rules that trip up new solvers: which way diagonal clues point, where an entry starts and stops, and why one row can legally hold two 5s.
- [Kakuro Unique Sums for Beginners: 3, 4, 16, and 17 in Two Cells](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-unique-sums/): Master the four 2-cell Kakuro unique sums (3, 4, 16, and 17) that start every beginner solve, learn the 10-minus-X mirror formula, and crack a 6x6 practice grid.
- [How to Cross-Reference Kakuro Clues: Solving Your First 2x2 Corners](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-cross-referencing-clues/): Learn beginner Kakuro cross-referencing: intersect 2-cell across and down clues to lock corner digits, calculate forced remainders, and solve without guessing.
- [Common Kakuro Mistakes Beginners Make and How to Avoid Them](https://motleyplay.com/posts/common-kakuro-mistakes/): Guessing, hidden duplicates, stale pencil marks, and addition slips ruin most beginner Kakuro grids. Here's how to catch each habit and stop it early.
- [Transitioning from Sudoku to Kakuro: What Changes?](https://motleyplay.com/posts/sudoku-to-kakuro/): Good at Sudoku but stuck on Kakuro? See which habits carry over, why the no-repeat rule resets at every black cell, and how Sudoku pairs map to unique sums.

## Kakuro Puzzle Design

- [How to Make a Kakuro Puzzle From Scratch](https://motleyplay.com/posts/how-to-make-kakuro/): Complete hub guide to constructing a valid Kakuro puzzle from scratch: 180-degree grid symmetry, fixing 2x2 deadly swaps, difficulty grading, and Python verification.
- [Designing a Kakuro Grid: 180° Symmetry, Run Lengths, and Black Cells](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-grid-design/): Learn Kakuro grid topology rules: 2-to-9 cell run bounds, orthogonal connectivity, 180-degree interior symmetry (N-r, N-c), and printable 7x7–15x15 PDF templates.
- [How to Make Sure Your Kakuro Has Exactly One Solution (Fixing 2x2 Swaps)](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-unique-solution/): Why fill-first Kakuro grids suffer from 2x2 deadly digit swaps, why magic blocks can't stop a pure swap, and how to prove and repair solution uniqueness.
- [How to Set Kakuro Difficulty: Technique, Not Grid Size](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-difficulty-levels/): Kakuro difficulty comes from the hardest deduction technique a grid forces, not its size. Grade a 7x7 as Medium, then refill the same layout so it requires a region count.
- [Build a Kakuro Solver and Generator in Python](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-solver-generator/): Write a fast Python Kakuro solver using 9-bit candidate masks and run-level filtering, then build a generator that repairs 2x2 swaps and grades human difficulty.
- [Designing Kakuro Grids That Hide an Answer](https://motleyplay.com/posts/kakuro-hidden-answers/): Design escape room Kakuro puzzles that reveal a secret lock code or page number: pre-lock target cells, avoid the zero and duplicate traps, and pace the reveal.

## Playable Puzzles

Free murder-mystery puzzles you can play in your browser: a logic grid, a Victorian cryptogram, a detective-themed connections board, and a mansion escape.

- [Death at Ravenscroft Manor: A Murder Mystery Logic Grid](https://motleyplay.com/games/mansion-murder-logic/): Four guests, four rooms, one dead lord. Solve a free murder-mystery logic grid in your browser using nine clues and pure deduction. No guessing.
- [The Detective's Maxim: A Victorian Cryptogram](https://motleyplay.com/games/victorian-cryptogram/): Crack a substitution cipher hiding a famous line from Sherlock Holmes. Type one letter and every match updates. Free to play in your browser.
- [Detective Clues: A Murder Mystery Connections Puzzle](https://motleyplay.com/games/detective-clues-connections/): Sixteen words, four hidden groups, four mistakes allowed. A detective-themed connections puzzle with a red herring or two. Free to play in your browser.
- [The Blackwood Estate: A Victorian Murder Escape](https://motleyplay.com/games/blackwood-estate-escape/): Locked in a Yorkshire manor with a body in the study. Crack two locks, test three alibis and name the killer in a free text-based escape game.
